Hook: Most knee pain has more options than you've been told.
Body:
Before recommending knee replacement, we ask: have all non-surgical options been explored? For many patients, the answer is no.

At Jeevisha, we evaluate before we treat. We discuss every option — including regenerative therapies, image-guided procedures, and physiotherapy — and recommend surgery only when it's truly the right call.

If you've been told you need knee surgery, consider a second opinion first.

Hook: Surgery isn't always the answer. Sometimes, your body is.
Body:
Regenerative medicine — including PRP, biologics, and stem-cell-based therapies — works by supporting the body's natural healing mechanisms.

It's not a miracle. It's measurable, evidence-based care for carefully selected patients.

If you'd like to understand whether regenerative therapy may be appropriate for your condition, a specialist evaluation is the first step.

Body:

Every patient is different. Outcomes depend on individual condition, evaluation, and adherence to the plan. But the option to explore non-surgical care is real.

Hook: 5 signs your back pain needs a specialist.
Body:
Most back pain resolves on its own. Some doesn't.

Warning signs that warrant a specialist evaluation:
1. Pain lasting more than 2 weeks
2. Tingling or numbness in legs
3. Pain that worsens at night or during sleep
4. Difficulty with daily movements
5. Pain that worsens despite rest

A specialist evaluation can identify whether your back pain is mechanical, nerve-related, or structural — and what the right approach should be.

Body:
Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy uses concentrated platelets from your own blood to support healing in damaged tissues — typically joints, tendons, or spinal discs.

The procedure:
1. A small blood draw (similar to a routine blood test)
2. Centrifugation to concentrate platelets
3. Image-guided injection into the target area

Same day. Usually 60-90 minutes total.

It's not appropriate for every condition or every patient. Evaluation matters.

At Jeevisha, every patient visit begins with three things:

1. We listen to your full story, not just symptoms.
2. We review your imaging together — explain what it shows, what it doesn't, and what it means.
3. We discuss every reasonable option, ranked by evidence — not by our preferred procedure.

Then we plan. Together.

This is what evidence-led, patient-first care actually looks like in practice.
